fixes.explanation: True, baker. Moses says, "Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and will no longer behave arrogantly." The whole people hear about it, and it shapes how they act. Verse 13 is easy to skim past when the verses right before it are so heavy. I'd say it's worth slowing down for.
The town doesn't come into this one, friend. Moses says a bribe "…twists the words of the righteous." It goes after their sight and their speech. Two things get hit, and neither one is the neighbors.

A golden calf, friend? I love the confidence. I once stamped a whole batch with the wrong shape and kept going like nothing happened, so I know that feeling. But this verse names a sacred pillar, and it says the LORD your God hates it. Moses has the Asherah pole in the verse right before, and the pillar is the one that follows.
Moses doesn't say that here, friend. First comes the checking: "…you must investigate it thoroughly." Then he says what to do if the report is true. Sending anybody anywhere isn't the first step.

A city of refuge isn't what this verse names, friend. Moses says you must go up to the place the LORD your God will choose. The LORD is the one who picks where it is. That's the whole answer, and it's a good one.

Elders are a fair guess, friend. I'd have guessed them too if I were rushing. But Moses says to go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who presides at that time. Priests and a judge, side by side. Then, he says, "Inquire of them, and they will give you a verdict in the case."

That's the reason, baker. Moses says, "…for the LORD has said, ‘You are never to go back that way again.’" The king must not acquire many horses for himself, and he must not send the people back to Egypt to get more. The reason Moses gives for that second part is what the LORD said.

True, baker. Moses says the king is to keep the instruction with him and read it all the days of his life. Then, he says, "…his heart will not be exalted above his countrymen…" (Deuteronomy 17:19-20). A king with a scroll that he reads every day, and a heart that stays low. I'd call that a good trade.

Growing borders sound nice, but Moses doesn't say that. He says it's so that the king and his sons "…may reign many years over his kingdom in Israel." The purpose he gives is about years on the throne. Land getting bigger isn't in the verse.
